data.title: Momentum Stocks: Geojit Financial Services, Patel Engineering, Wanbury gain up to 7% on sheer momentum
data.description:
Buzzing Stocks

In a market short on fresh triggers, several stocks quietly grabbed attention on November 27, driven by technical breakouts, strong price action, and sustained buying interest.

The selected stocks are showing strong upward momentum, trading well above their key short- to medium-term moving averages, which indicates a positive trend in the near term.

Geojit Financial Services shares surged 7.46 percent to Rs 76.66 and were trading above their 30-day, 50-day, 150-day and 200-day simple moving averages (SMAs) of Rs 71.34, Rs 74.16, Rs 75.61 and Rs 72.51, respectively.

Patel Engineering share price gained 7.34 percent to Rs 26.03 and was trading above its 30-day and 50-day SMAs of Rs 24.25 and Rs 25.01, but below its 150-day and 200-day SMAs of Rs 27.53 and Rs 27.31, respectively.

Wanbury shares advanced 7.33 percent to Rs 200.48 and were trading above their 30-day and 50-day SMAs of Rs 186.78 and Rs 197.47, but below their 150-day and 200-day SMAs of Rs 248.45 and Rs 248.88, respectively.

Onyx Biotec shares declined 3.93 percent to Rs 35.70 and were trading below their 30-day, 50-day, 150-day and 200-day simple moving averages (SMAs) of Rs 37.16, Rs 37.66, Rs 37.58 and Rs 37, respectively.

Equippp Social Impact Technologies share price fell 3.05 percent to Rs 20 and was trading below its 30-day, 50-day and 150-day SMAs of Rs 20.63, Rs 21.49 and Rs 20.76, respectively, but above its 200-day SMA of Rs 19.79.

Golden Tobacco shares shed 2.64 percent to Rs 21.37 and were trading below their 30-day, 50-day, 150-day and 200-day SMAs of Rs 21.95, Rs 22.66, Rs 24.60 and Rs 25.33, respectively.

Several stocks touched fresh 52-week high, highlighting persistent buying interest in the market. Notable names that hit new high included stocks of BEML, Action Construction, MCX India, Navin Fluorine, Welspun Living, Glenmark Pharma, Anand Rathi, Mankind Pharma, DLF, Laurus Labs, Tech Mahindra, Prestige Estate.

Nifty IT index snapped its four-day winning streak to fall 1.5% on November 27 due to various reasons, including profit booking and rise in Nasdaq futures.

At 10:15 am on November 27, Nifty IT index was trading 1.4% lower at 32,955 with Mphasis, HCL Technologies, Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) leading the losses by declining 2.2%-2.6%. The sectoral index rose nearly 8% in the previous four-session rally.

"Nifty IT is currently testing its long-term descending trendline resistance at 33,000–33,300. The formation of a Golden Cross, coupled with a rising RSI at 63.42 and early signs of improvement in Relative Strength (RS) against Nifty 50, indicates a strengthening technical structure. A decisive weekly close above the trendline, supported by higher volumes, could pave the way towards 35,500 and subsequently 38,000–39,000, marking a potential reversal of the prolonged corrective phase. The 30,100–30,600 zone remains a key support area," said PL Capital.

Meanwhile, sentiment around artificial intelligence stabilised after a volatile week.

Major Asian indices were mixed in early trade, with most of them in green, tracking gains in US stock futures.

Related Stories

  • Momentum Stocks: Geojit Financial Services, Patel Engineering, Wanbury gain up to 7% on sheer moment...
  • Waaree Renewable Technologies shares surge 13% after 120 MWp solar project win

US equity futures rose Thursday night as investors wrapped up a volatile week of trading on Thanksgiving Day. However, the relief in stocks failed to sustain and the US indices came under pressure.

Investors are cautious while taking risks in artificial intelligence stocks due to the doubts hovering around debt financing, signs of moderation in capital expenditure, and a slowdown in data centre development after the US mid-term elections, according to CNBC.

South Korea's technology-heavy Kospi and Japan's Topix First Section were the top gainers among indices, up almost 2% and over 1%, respectively. China's CSI 300 index fell 0.4% and was the major laggard among its peers.

Indian IT shares have been reacting adversely to surge in AI-related stocks as investments are being poured into the burgeoning technology.

Shares of Waaree Renewable Technologies surged 13 percent to Rs 777.5 in morning trade on Friday, November 27, after the company secured an order for a 120 megawatt-peak (MWp) solar project. The stock was among the top smallcap gainers, taking the company’s market capitalisation to about Rs 8,050 crore.

The Waaree Energies subsidiary said it received the letter of award after market hours on Thursday. Under the turnkey contract, Waaree Renewable Technologies will supply the solar modules and carry out the engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) work for the project.

A domestic private limited company awarded the contract, and the project is scheduled for completion in the financial year ending March 2028. Waaree Renewable Technologies did not disclose the customer’s name or the contract value. It said the order did not constitute a related-party transaction and that its promoter, promoter group and group companies had no interest in the customer.

The stock’s double-digit rise came as smallcaps and midcaps advanced even as the benchmark Nifty 50 edged lower. The Nifty Smallcap 100 rose 0.9 percent to 19,547.8 and the Nifty Midcap 100 gained 0.9 percent to 62,309.9, while the Nifty 50 slipped 0.2 percent to 25,841.

Friday’s rally pared Waaree Renewable Technologies’ losses for the year. The stock was still down 20 percent year to date, compared with a 1.2 percent decline in the Nifty 50.

September-quarter profit fell 30%

Waaree Renewable Technologies reported a net profit of Rs 82 crore for the September quarter of FY27, down 30 percent from Rs 116 crore a year earlier. Revenue from operations rose 36.5 percent to Rs 1,057.8 crore from Rs 775 crore.

Operating earnings grew much more slowly than revenue. Earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) rose 1.3 percent to Rs 160 crore from Rs 158 crore, while the EBITDA margin narrowed by five percentage points to 15 percent.

data.title: Price Action: Zydus Lifesciences slips on USFDA CRL; Syrma SGS, Avalon Technologies gain after JPMorgan upgrades
data.description:
Buzzing Stocks:

Stock-specific action remained in focus on Dalal Street on November 27 with investors reacting to brokerage recommendations and regulatory developments.

Share price of Zydus Lifesciences fell more than 1 percent after its US subsidiary, Zydus Therapeutics Inc., received a Complete Response Letter (CRL) from the US Food and Drug Administration (USFDA) for its New Drug Application (NDA) for Saroglitazar. The letter relates to the company's resolution plan addressing observations raised during the October 2026 inspection of its Moraiya facility.

Shares of Syrma SGS and Avalon Technologies rose nearly 2% each after JPMorgan upgraded the stocks to 'neutral'.

Lemon Tree Hotels share price rose nearly 1 percent after company announced the opening of Keys Select by Lemon Tree Hotels in Pali. With this addition, the group's operational portfolio in Maharashtra has expanded to 17 hotels, while another 15 properties are in the development pipeline. The property operates under a franchise agreement, further strengthening the group's presence and expanding its development pipeline across the region.

On the sectoral front, Nifty PSU Bank and Metal indices rose more than 1 percent each, while IT index shed 1.6%.

Broader markets traded higher, with the Nifty Midcap and Smallcap indices gaining nearly 1 percent each.

Market breadth remained positive on the BSE, with 2314 shares advancing against 995 declining, while 196 stocks remained unchanged.

data.title: Mahanadi Coalfields shares make flat listing at 2% discount to IPO price; here’s how to trade Coal India unit
data.description:
Mahanadi Coalfields shares were listed on the exchanges on November 27.

Shares of Coal India unit Mahanadi Coalfields fell more than 2 percent in their trading debut on Friday, following a 1.52-times subscription to its initial public offering (IPO) in the primary market between November 19 and 23.

Shares of Mahanadi Coalfields were listed at Rs 133.15 per share on the BSE, a discount of 2.10 percent. The company's market capitalisation post-listing of its shares stood at Rs 88,123.50 crore.

On the NSE, the shares of the company were listed at Rs 134 per share, discount of 1.47 percent. The Rs 8,981 crore initial share sale had a price band of Rs 129-136 per share.

Earlier, the company raised Rs 2,295 crore from anchor investors.

The proposed listing is part of Coal India's broader plan to unlock value from its subsidiaries through the capital markets.

MCL is the third Coal India subsidiary to tap the public markets this year. Coal India has already listed Bharat Coking Coal Ltd in January, while the IPO of Central Mine Planning & Design Institute Ltd concluded in March.

Incorporated in 1992, MCL produced 218.31 million tonnes of coal in FY26, accounting for around 22.4 per cent of India's total non-coking coal production, according to the Crisil report cited in the offer documents.

It is also the largest coal-producing subsidiary of Coal India, contributing over 28 per cent to the state-owned company's total coal production in FY26.

Coal India accounts for more than 80 per cent of the country's domestic coal output.

data.title: Sensex falls 200 pts, Nifty near 25,850: Profit booking among key factors behind market decline
data.description:
Stock market news today: Sensex, Nifty see profit booking in trade.

The equity benchmarks traded lower on Friday amid profit booking after recent rally.

At around 9:30 a.m., the Sensex was down 187.11 points or 0.22 percent at 84,141.48, while the broader Nifty declined to 25,855.65, down 28.85 points or 0.11 percent.

Key factors behind market decline

1) Profit booking: Profit booking emerged at higher levels as investors locked in gains. Nifty and Sensex are up ‌0.3% ⁠each so far this week, consolidating after a blistering surge of 14.2% and 14.8%, respectively, over the last four weeks.

2) Elevated crude oil prices: Brent ​crude futures ​hovered ⁠around $96 per barrel as ongoing attacks on tankers ​in the Strait of ​Hormuz ⁠and Saudi energy infrastructure heightened concerns over oil exports from ⁠the ​conflict-hit region.

Shares of Kalyan Jewellers India rose 3.3 percent to Rs 661 in morning trade on Friday, November 27, after HSBC said jewellery demand remained strong despite a high base. The brokerage also cited the growth potential of the retailer’s affordable gold jewellery brand, Akshaya Thanga Maligai (ATM).

Kalyan Jewellers was among the top midcap gainers, with a market capitalisation of about Rs 68,300 crore. The stock has gained 36.9 percent so far this year, while the benchmark Nifty 50 has declined 1.2 percent.

HSBC has a Buy rating on Kalyan Jewellers and a target price of Rs 830 per share, implying about 30 percent upside from Thursday’s close. The brokerage highlighted ATM’s competitive making charges and said strong execution at the brand could lift earnings above its current estimates, which exclude ATM’s contribution.

The stock also rallied earlier this week, after Moneycontrol reported that Kalyan Jewellers was in talks with several private equity firms, including former investor Warburg Pincus, to raise close to Rs 2,000 crore through minority stake sales in its subsidiaries Candere and ATM.

A deal with Warburg Pincus would bring the private equity firm back into the Kalyan group more than two years after it completed its exit from the listed retailer in August 2024. Warburg Pincus invested about Rs 1,700 crore in two rounds between 2014 and 2017, helping Kalyan Jewellers expand from its South Indian base into northern and western India as well as overseas markets.

Kalyan Jewellers Q2 profit rises 64%

Kalyan Jewellers reported a 63.6 percent year-on-year rise in consolidated net profit to Rs 427 crore for the September quarter, from Rs 260.51 crore a year earlier. The quarter included a Rs 73 crore exceptional gain from the sale of a non-core land parcel. Excluding that gain, net profit rose nearly 36 percent to about Rs 354 crore.

Consolidated revenue rose 31.4 percent to Rs 10,323 crore from Rs 7,856 crore a year earlier, crossing the Rs 10,000 crore mark. Following the results, UBS maintained its Buy rating on the stock with a target price of Rs 900 per share.
